findings_addressed.oracle: The helper creates exactly 3 named mutexes each held for 400 ms (_TRANSIENT_MUTEX_LIFETIME_MS). The monitor runs at 100 ms poll (_FAST_POLL_INTERVAL_MS). After the monitor's first sweep completes (signalled by |OpenProcess| in the error log), _poll_log_for_pid_mutex polls the object log for lines where the pipe-delimited owner_pid field equals helper_proc.pid AND the object-name field contains 'IntellicrackAudit3U7'. The helper PID is never injected into the monitor; it is present in the log only if the monitor independently enumerated the handle. _assert_log_entry_fields then verifies parts[1]=='Mutant', parts[3]==str(helper_pid), and parts[5]=='created' against the actual log line.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In kernel_object_monitor.ps1, change 'Start-Sleep -Milliseconds $PollIntervalMilliseconds' back to 'Start-Sleep -Seconds 3'. With 3 s polling the monitor's next sweep fires after all three 400 ms mutexes are already released; _poll_log_for_pid_mutex returns [] because no log lines match helper_pid; the 'assert matching_lines' assertion fails.

findings_addressed.oracle: Before termination, _get_descendant_pids runs a fresh pwsh process that queries Win32_Process via Get-CimInstance and walks the full process tree from proc.pid using BFS over ParentProcessId. The list of descendant PIDs is captured while the monitor is alive. After _terminate(proc), _pid_is_alive is called for proc.pid (parent must be gone) and for every descendant PID (children/grandchildren must also be gone). survivor_pids collects any that are still alive and asserts it is empty.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In kernel_object_monitor.ps1, add a 'Start-Process pwsh -ArgumentList "-NoProfile","-Command","Start-Sleep 300" -NoNewWindow' call inside the monitor's main loop. The spawned child pwsh is not killed when the parent is terminated; _get_descendant_pids captures the child's PID before kill; _pid_is_alive returns True for that PID after kill; survivor_pids is non-empty and the assertion fails.

notes: G0012: Replaced the vacuous 20000-iteration/2000ms helper (which would still be caught at 3s polling) with an exactly-3-mutex/400ms helper. The 400ms mutex lifetime is shorter than the legacy 3s cadence, so at 3s polling all three mutexes are released before the first poll fires. The independent oracle is the helper PID in the log's owner_pid field. Extracted _poll_log_for_pid_mutex, _assert_log_entry_fields, and _run_mutex_helper_and_collect to stay within ruff's PLR0914 (<=15 local variables) and PLW0717 (<=5 try-clause statements) limits. G0013: Replaced the tautological parent-PID-only check (which trivially passes after proc.kill()) with a WMI-based descendant enumeration. _get_descendant_pids does a BFS over Win32_Process.ParentProcessId before termination, then _pid_is_alive checks each captured PID after kill. This catches the realistic breakage where the script spawns detached background pwsh processes that outlive the parent. POST-WORKFLOW FIX (2026-06-23): (1) DELETED test_script_no_orphan_pwsh_after_terminate (G0013, tautological) as a VACUOUS gate - kernel_object_monitor.ps1 spawns NO child processes (verified: no Start-Process/Start-Job/Invoke-Command -AsJob), so child_pids is always [] and the survivor assertion always passes regardless of any real script breakage; it only gates hypothetical future orphan-spawning code. Removed its two now-orphaned helpers (_get_descendant_pids, _pid_is_alive) and the now-unused json/cast/run imports. (2) test_script_captures_transient_mutex (G0012) was FLAKY (genuinely falsifiable per the reviewer, but 3 sequential 400ms mutexes vs container sweep timing meant a sweep could miss the short windows). Fixed deterministically WITHOUT weakening: the helper now holds all 3 mutexes SIMULTANEOUSLY for a single 2000ms window (was 3x400ms sequential). 2000ms < the 3000ms legacy cadence preserves falsifiability (a 3s-poll monitor's next sweep after creation fires after the window closed -> misses all -> RED under the regression); a continuously-present 2s window gives the 100ms monitor many full sweep cycles -> robust capture. NOTE: could not lengthen sequential mutexes (total window would exceed 3s and a slow sweep would land in a later mutex's window, breaking falsifiability) - simultaneous-hold keeps total window < 3s.
